griffiths-gnat.shows: Closest style only: a parachute dry from above, its body lying on the surface with hackle fibres spread in the film and dimples at their tips. The Gnat's palmered fibres meet the film the same way, all along the body.

parachute-adams.author: Murray's Fly Shop
parachute-adams.shows: #16 Mr. Rapidan Parachute (same construction as the Parachute Adams) after the floatant test, low side view with its reflection. The hackle disc lies on the film, the body is flush with the surface, the tail fibres lie on the water and the post is upright.

parachute-adams.author: Murray's Fly Shop

rackelhanen.author: Nick Thomas (The Global FlyFisher)
rackelhanen.shows: Closest style (a poly-yarn sedge, not the Rackelhanen itself): low side view, the shaggy yarn wing over a dark head, the body in the film, a dark reflection under the whole fly, the tippet's bright meniscus leading off to the left.
rackelhanen.compare: how it sits: what is in, through and above the film

red-tag.author: CosmicJohn (Box of Rain, Substack)
red-tag.shows: Closest style only: a collar-hackled dry on still water (this one has a long tail, which the Red Tag lacks). It shows how the lower hackle fibres pierce the film and the bend hangs below. Without a tail the rear would sit lower.

red-tag.author: J. Castwell ("Flies Only", FlyAnglers Online; posted by Bruce_Norikane)
red-tag.shows: Closest style only: a peacock-bodied hackled dry from below. Dark herl body and hook silhouette, hackle dimples, hook bend below the surface.
red-tag.compare: how it sits: what is in, through and above the film

royal-wulff.author: Scientific Anglers magazine advertisement (photographer not named); scanned and posted by oldster
royal-wulff.shows: Royal Wulff on water in a Scientific Anglers advertisement (likely staged): riding on the hackle and tail, the body clear of the film, the tail fibres on the surface, the hook bend just at the film with its reflection, the white wings upright, the tippet leading off the eye.

royal-wulff.author: J. Castwell ("Flies Only", FlyAnglers Online; posted by Bruce_Norikane)
royal-wulff.shows: Peacock-bodied, pale-winged hackled dry (Royal Coachman type, closest style to the Royal Wulff) from below: hackle fibres radiating and dimpling the film, the tail in a round dimple, the hook bend below the surface.

royal-wulff.author: CosmicJohn (Box of Rain, Substack)
royal-wulff.shows: Hackled winged dry on still water (same style, not a Wulff). The body is clear of the film, the lower hackle and tail tips are in it and the bend goes through the surface.

stimulator.author: dataminer007 (Flickr)
stimulator.shows: A Stimulator (yellow abdomen, orange thorax, grizzly front hackle, elk wing and tail) on calm blue water at eye level, eye left, tippet lying on the surface: the fly stands on its palmered and front hackle, the abdomen clear of the film, the hook bend reaching down to the surface, wing raised low over the back. Looks freshly dressed (high).
stimulator.compare: how it sits: what is in, through and above the film

stimulator.author: WiFlyFisher.com (no photographer named)
stimulator.shows: The same two flies seen from almost straight underneath: the CDC & Elk's whole underside (body, CDC fibres and the spread hair wing) pressed into the film; the Royal Trude (collar hackle, hair down-wing) shows its body and hackle points dimpling the film. Wayback copy (live file 404). Closest style: Royal Trude (Trude-family ancestor of the Stimulator) from below: hackle points dimpling the film.

streaking-caddis.author: Hans Weilenmann (The Global FlyFisher)
streaking-caddis.shows: CDC & Elk (the exact pattern, tied by its originator) on rippled water, low three-quarter view, eye right: the CDC body and its fibres lie in the film, the hook bend hangs just below the surface, the deer-hair wing lies back low over the body with its tips trailing at or near the water, the square-cut butts stand up at the head, the tippet leaves the eye along the surface. Closest style: a hackle-less deer-hair-wing caddis with square-cut hair butts at the head; the Streaking Caddis's head is spun and much denser.
